title: Ann Berry on the Importance of Learning AI
summary: Barry speaks with Ann Berry, founder and managing partner of Threadneedle. They discuss her path from Goldman Sachs M&A and private equity to running a hospitality services company through the pandemic. They also discuss Ann's early-stage bets on AI and deepfake detection, and surveying the expanding IPO landscape. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Airbnb Surges 12% as Growth Accelerates and Outlook Rises | Closing Bell

title: Hedge Funds Fled Bullish Oil Bets Ahead of Election Day Drop
summary: Hedge funds cut bullish crude bets by the most since June as the US and Iran struck rare de-escalatory notes, positioning them to profit from the selloff after the Democratic sweep of Congress.

title: Gold Extends Drop on Stronger-Than-Expected US Employment Data
summary: Gold fell after a hot US nonfarm payrolls print added fuel to speculations that the Federal Reserve will seek to raise interest rates to contain inflation.

title: Wall Street Grapples With $5.7 Trillion Rout as AI Bets Unwind
summary: Months of unease over Wall Street’s artificial-intelligence boom erupted into a global market convulsion this week, opening a dangerous new chapter for the investment frenzy that has helped power stock prices, corporate spending and economic growth.

title: Chip Stocks Climb After Rout, But AI Doubts Linger: Markets Wrap
summary: A rebound in chipmakers propped up the stock market as dip buyers emerged despite economic data that reinforced speculation the Federal Reserve will boost rates in December.

title: Retail Traders Cautiously Buy Stocks After Worst Rout Since 2025
summary: Retail traders, the stock market’s most avid dip buyers since the pandemic, were among the investors buying on Friday after US equities had their worst day since 2025. But their typical enthusiasm was nowhere to be found.

title: Oil Swings as Traders Parse Iran War De-Escalation Prospects
summary: Oil swung in a choppy session, as traders weighed progress on de-escalation in the Iran war.

title: Braskem Shareholders Pull Funding Offer as Debt Talks Stall
summary: Talks between Brazil’s Braskem SA and its creditors regarding an out-of-court debt rework have soured, with shareholders taking a proposed capital injection key to a deal off the table, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: Copper Moves Lower as US Election Undermines AI and Tariff Trade
summary: Copper slumped to its lowest since July as a political shakeup in Washington threatened to blunt two key bullish drivers: the rapid buildout of AI infrastructure, and the risk of US import tariffs on the metal.

title: US Bonds’ Election Rally Skids to Halt After Strong Jobs Data
summary: The Treasury market pared a steep weekly advance after strong October employment data revived wagers on a Federal Reserve interest-rate hike next month.

title: Wall Street Sees US Hitting $41.1 Trillion Debt Cap in February
summary: Wall Street strategists are bracing for the US Treasury to hit against its borrowing limit as early as February, triggering the need for extraordinary measures before it faces a funding crunch in late 2027.

title: Don't Think Social Security Going Away: Lusardi
summary: Annamaria Lusardi, senior fellow at the Stanford Institute for Economic Policy & Research and TIAA Financial Literacy co-author, joins Scarlet Fu and Tom Keene on "Bloomberg Money." They discuss the future of Social Security and retirement in the US. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: I Don't Own Bonds, Comfortable With Volatility: Moore
summary:
Kate Moore, CIO of Citi Wealth, joins Scarlet Fu and Tom Keene on "Bloomberg Money." Kate Moore discusses her personal investment strategy. She explains that she doesn't personally own bonds and that she is comfortable with volatility in the market.
 (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Supreme Court to Hear Goldman Sachs’ Bankruptcy Arbitration Bid
summary: The US Supreme Court agreed to review a request by Goldman Sachs on whether bankruptcy courts can override arbitration agreements, setting up a high-stakes test of the Federal Arbitration Act’s reach.

title: Quick Mart IPO Draws Strong Demand as Kenyan Listings Pick Up
summary: Quick Mart Plc saw demand for shares in its initial public offering exceed the number available by almost 23% as Kenya’s second-biggest supermarket chain concluded the nation’s second IPO of the year.

title: Anatomy of a Selloff: Sudden Chain Reaction Rattles Wall Street
summary: It took around 24 hours for Wall Street’s response to the US midterm elections to turn negative. Once it did, it set in motion a chain reaction of selling that moved considerably faster.

title: AI Trade Rebounds After Historic Rout for Tech Stocks
